## What is happening
**The spike isn't in sales. It's in the demand feed the supply team plans from.**

- **What the feed shows:** weeks 15–18 (6 Apr – 3 May) are 73.9% above the prior 8-week average, at 350 units a week.
- **What the tills show:** 209 units a week against 201 before, up 3.7%.
- **Why they differ:** every store got the same weekly factor, which real demand doesn't do. These are manual demand overrides:
  - week 15 ×1.35, week 16 ×1.5, week 17 ×1.72 and week 18 ×2.2
  - entered by Sam Patel (Demand Planning) on 2 Apr 2026
  - reason given: "Uplift ahead of the Kimberly-Clark Crawler Nappies TV campaign (supplier advised a mid-April launch)"
  - due for review on 30 Apr 2026 and **still active**

**Real sales:** POS for the 28 days to 7 May was AUD 23.3K. That is up 2.5% on last year (AUD +576) and up 0.7% on the prior 28 days. Other Crawler Nappies brands were flat (0%) year on year, and Huggies' share rose 0.6 pts to 44.8%. The class is in line with last year and with its market. The campaign uplift the overrides assumed doesn't show at the tills.

Weekly reported demand vs POS units (from the reconciliation):

| Week starting | POS units | Reported units | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 Mar | 209 | 209 | 0% |
| 6 Apr | 197 | 266 | +35% |
| 13 Apr | 228 | 342 | +50% |
| 20 Apr | 228 | 392 | +72% |
| 27 Apr | 182 | 400 | +120% |
| 4 May (partial) | 124 | 124 | 0% |

## What we tested
| Hypothesis | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Demand override in the feed | Feed +73.9% vs POS +3.7%; same factor in every store | Confirmed |
| Market | Brand +2.5% vs market 0% | Confirmed (moving with the market) |
| Price / volume | Units +2.5%, ASP +0.1% | Ruled out |
| Step change by week | 209 vs 202 units a week; steady | Ruled out |
| Promotion | Promo mix 14.3% vs 14.1% last year | Ruled out |
| Competitor price | Average price gap moved −0.62 pts | Ruled out |
| Supply | On-time-in-full deliveries (DIFOT) fell from 93.5% to 67.5% (54% in week 18); out of stock 2.2% vs 1.7% for the market | Risk, not a cause |

**Supply risk:** deliveries are failing, but stores still hold stock, so it hasn't cost sales yet. If supply has been ordering against the inflated feed while DIFOT drops, the gap between what was ordered and what stores receive and sell will be distorted over the next few weeks.

## What to do
1. **Demand Planning:** review or remove overrides DOV-26-0415 to DOV-26-0418. They are past their 30 Apr review date and still active.
2. **Category:** check with Kimberly-Clark whether the TV campaign ran or was delayed. POS shows no lift.
3. **Supply:** escalate Crawler Nappies DIFOT, which was 54% in week 18 against 92.8% for Huggies' other classes.
4. **Data:** the daily forecast shows an online uplift of +82.7% from 18 May. Its demand history runs 101% above POS, so treat that uplift as unconfirmed.
